data.question: Do official Lean and Nanoda reject three single-record invalid universe declarations while accepting byte-identical matched controls?
data.versions: Lean4.34.1 ARM64, Nanoda3a24072, compiled lean4export076e8e5, NDJSON3.1.0; current binary/parser/source hashes checked against retained profile.
data.commands: run_process.py matrix 300 python3 run_matrix.py. Twelve exact invocations: direct Lean --run raw Replay.lean and nanoda_bin with per-case config. Full commands/streams/exits/durations retained per cell.
data.sample: P1/Pbad (undeclared parameter), M1/Mbad (lowered max level), I1/Ibad (imax-to-max error at zero). Three expected ACCEPT controls and three expected REJECT candidates; six cases x two validators.
data.controls: Exit status alone is insufficient. Official REJECT requires the expected undefined-universe or declaration-type-mismatch diagnostic after exact parsed-object prints. Nanoda uses assertion panics for invalid inputs: classify an expected all_uparams_defined assertion from infer_sort or def_eq assertion from assert_def_eq as REJECT_VIA_ASSERTION, preserving the nonzero code and panic text. Distinguish these intentional rejection paths from parser/unsupported failures, timeouts, unrelated diagnostic panics and crashes. Valid controls require exit0 and explicit one-declaration completion, with no stderr. Any unknown failure is diagnosed/repaired within this item, never silently mapped to REJECT. Reuse raw Replay.lean: print parsed params, type and value before empty-environment trust0 kernel replay; require exact equality to cases.json for every case, including rejected ones. Nanoda parser directly inserts raw param/max/imax levels (source bound by observed hashes); error attribution must reach the intended checker guard. Both consume exactly the same input bytes verified before and after.
